jobs.description: Adjunct Clinical Faculty - Medical-Surgical Nursing (General Nursing) Mississippi Christian University of Nursing invites applications for adjunct clinical faculty in Medical-Surgical Nursing. jobs.description: Department:The successful candidate will be a regular faculty member in Physics and Astronomy.Job Summary:The Department of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Mississippi seeks highly qualified candidates for a tenure-track faculty position in physics education research. The role involves teaching (undergraduate and graduate courses), research (including supervision of students, especially in projects leading to master’s and doctoral degrees), and service (to the department, university, community, profession).Job Description:The Department of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Mississippi (UM) invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position in physics education research (PER) at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor. This position is supported in part by an endowment to honor F. Douglas and Cora Beal Shields and represents a significant institutional investment in establishing PER as a strategic area of excellence. The purpose of the endowment is to recruit and retain outstanding faculty for the Department of Physics and Astronomy; to advance the understanding of physics pedagogy and contribute to the field of PER; to raise the quality of instruction across the department; and to seed a new research area with meaningful doctoral production. This position offers a unique opportunity to establish a nationally visible PER group at a flagship R1 university with strong undergraduate and graduate physics programs and to help define the future direction of PER at the University of Mississippi. The position includes a competitive salary and a startup package. Income from the endowment will be used to provide funds for research and creative activity, including but not limited to support for personnel (graduate teaching and research assistants, undergraduate learning assistants), operational support for scientific studies, travel to conferences, and hosting visitors and workshops. There are also opportunities for collaboration and support in connection with UM’s Center for Excellence in Teaching and Learning, Center for Math and Science Education, Center for STEM Learning, and Institute for Data Science. The Physics and Astronomy faculty are eager to attract a driven, energetic colleague who can help to craft a long-term vision for growing out PER in the department. Ideally, the new faculty member will be a proselytizer for active learning and a catalyst for extending modern, evidence-based practices. Like all our tenure-track faculty, this person must also excel at mentoring graduate students and providing them with research opportunities that lead to the Ph.D. degree. The search committee’s aperture for evaluating the candidates is quite wide. Applications are encouraged from researchers working in all areas of PER and at all career stages. The department is open to recruiting an emerging scholar or an established researcher who could be hired with an accelerated tenure clock. A Ph.D. in Physics or a closely related field is required. Candidates should have relevant experience beyond the doctoral degree, a strong record of publication or impact in the field, demonstrated potential for establishing and sustaining a nationally recognized research program, and well-conceived plans to pursue external funding opportunities. The successful candidate is expected to establish an active and independent research program, teach effectively at both the undergraduate and graduate levels, and contribute to the service missions of the department and university. Applications should be submitted online via the Faculty Career Site portal, which is accessible from https://olemiss.edu/hr/um-careers/ by clicking through to External Applicants > Faculty Openings. jobs.description: Department: Mechanical Engineering Job Summary: The Department of Mechanical Engineering at the University of Mississippi (Ole Miss), Oxford, Mississippi, invites applications for a full-time Instructional Assistant Professor of Mechanical Engineering. Candidates from all areas of mechanical engineering will be considered. Candidates with expertise and teaching capacity in core undergraduate areas such as materials, mechanics, dynamics, thermal-fluid sciences, design, engineering systems, hands-on laboratories, or related mechanical engineering topics are especially encouraged to apply. The successful candidate will join a collegial department committed to rigorous engineering education, student success, laboratory safety, continuous improvement, and preparing graduates for professional practice and advanced study. jobs.description: Purpose of the Role and Scope of Responsibility: Prepares for and teaches Workforce Industrial Plumbing courses and conducts labs as assigned by the Dean of Workforce Education. Instructors are responsible for teaching students in our training programs in the classroom and hands-on lab settings, ensuring that they gain the knowledge and skills that are required for entry-level employment in their chosen field. Instructors are also responsible for sound educational practices and the academic development of each student. Instructors will also manage their classroom environment and promote a positive and engaging learning experience, providing support, tutoring, and other assistance as needed. Instructors are to “model" the professional behaviors, language, and activities expected of our students. Duties and Responsibilities: Must have exposure and knowledge of the NCCER requirements Teaches assigned courses in Skilled Trades as scheduled in accordance with current department approved course descriptions, course outlines, syllabi, and procedures. Assists, as appropriate, in the maintenance of instructional materials and laboratory facilities. Assists in the maintenance of course descriptions, course outlines, and syllabi. Consults in development and updates course descriptions routinely based on industry changes or trends, advisory committee suggestions, and assessment results. Employs appropriate assessment techniques to measure student performance in achieving course goals and objectives. Communicates progress in the course to students in a timely manner. Determines and submits students' grades in accordance with established college workforce department policies and procedures. Advises potential or current students within the discipline. Ensures classroom lectures contain essential curricular components; have appropriate content and pedagogy; and reflect current trends. Participates, as appropriate, in additional duties and responsibilities based upon the expertise of the individual and the needs of the department, division, or College. Works assigned schedule, exhibits regular and predictable attendance. Utilize classroom and lab instruction, student assessment mechanisms, and classroom management techniques to provide an engaged classroom experience to students. Ensure that each student has been presented with the material to successfully meet the learning objectives of each course within a student’s program of study Ensure that instructional materials and equipment are ready for student use, sufficient in quantity, properly maintained and in working order prior to class time Participate in ongoing faculty assessment and professional development activities to ensure an active and engaged classroom experience for all students; maintain required certification and license Actively participate in meetings, review and analyze assessment data, compile reports, and meet academic and administrative deadlines Ensure campus compliance with all federal, state, and regulatory bodies’ guidelines, along with internal policies of the company Other duties as assigned
